lines.trans: Whoa! Why is my table plan pulling like a boat sail on the high seas?!
Hold both bottom corners tight, Ernesto, a huge gust just came through the arch!

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: Look up! Cord one of the paper lanterns is spinning around with cord two!
Oh no, my glasses are slipping off my forehead: let me grab them with one hand!
Ernesto, DO NOT LET GO OF THE RIGHT CORNER OF THE PAPER!

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: Whoosh! Come back here, tables one through seven! Stop flying toward the tree!
I almost caught it by the herb pots: watch out, it caught a second breeze!
It is gliding past table four, turns left, and heads straight for the courtyard fountain!
Not into the stone fountain! That is washable blue pen ink, not waterproof paint!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Jump left, Clara! Grab the dry corner before it lands face down in the water!

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Indicates position or movement downward.

examples.text: La cocina está abajo.
examples.trans: The kitchen is downstairs.

examples.text: Te espero abajo en el patio.
examples.trans: I will wait for you downstairs in the courtyard.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.text: Acabo de llegar del mercado.
examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

examples.text: Pero ¿adónde vas, Lidia? ¿Qué haces así vestida?
examples.trans: Where are you going, Lidia? What are you doing dressed like that?

examples.text: Hablamos de adónde en la oficina.
examples.trans: We talk about where to at the office.

agarrar.gloss: to grip; to stick; to take hold

meanings.en: to grip; to stick; to take hold
meanings.note: Said of paint or glue adhering to dry wood, as well as gripping with the hand.

examples.text: La pintura nueva agarra muy bien sobre madera seca.
examples.trans: Fresh paint sticks very well on dry wood.

examples.text: Agarra fuerte el otro extremo de la mesa.
examples.trans: Grip the other end of the table firmly.

meanings.note: Feminine noun that takes el in the singular before stressed initial /a/ (el agua fría).

examples.text: Quiero un vaso de agua fría.
examples.trans: I want a glass of cold water.

examples.text: El agua de la ducha sale caliente.
examples.trans: The shower water comes out hot.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Alto y claro means 'loud and clear'.

examples.text: Es una pieza alta.
examples.trans: It is a tall piece.

examples.text: Alto y claro. ¿Estás junto a la fuentecita de piedra?
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you beside the little stone fountain?

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Architectural stone archway or violin bow.

examples.text: El arco está aquí.
examples.trans: The arch is here.

examples.text: Vemos los arcos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the archs from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.text: Las habitaciones están arriba.
examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.

examples.text: Mira arriba hacia el balcón.
examples.trans: Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb for catching a thrown object or something blown by the wind.

examples.text: ¡Atrapa la punta de la cuerda antes de que caiga en la fuente!
examples.trans: Catch the end of the cord before it falls into the fountain!

examples.text: Casi atrapo el cartel de papel junto a las macetas de menta.
examples.trans: I almost caught the paper poster beside the mint pots.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.text: ¡Ay, casi olvido el paraguas!
examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!

examples.text: ¡Ay, qué susto me has dado!
examples.trans: Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.text: Es una pieza azul.
examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Everyday word for any large boat or ship (barco de vela = sailing ship).

examples.text: El plano de papel flotó en la fuente como un barco blanco.
examples.trans: The paper plan floated in the fountain like a white boat.

examples.text: Su tío trabajaba en los barcos del puerto de Valencia.
examples.trans: His uncle worked on the boats in the port of Valencia.

meanings.note: Quedarse blanco means 'to go pale'.

examples.text: Es una pieza blanca.
examples.trans: It is a white piece.

examples.text: Mira, hay un sobre blanco doblado en el asa.
examples.trans: Look, there is a folded white envelope on the handle.

meanings.note: Also denotes the pouring lip or opening of a jug or tunnel.

examples.text: La boca está aquí.
examples.trans: The mouth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las bocas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mouths from the door.

meanings.note: Denotes a gentle, pleasant wind, especially from the sea or through a shaded courtyard.

examples.text: Una brisa fresca de tarde entraba por la ventana abierta.
examples.trans: A cool afternoon breeze was coming through the open window.

examples.text: Bajo el limonero siempre corre una brisa muy agradable.
examples.trans: Under the lemon tree there is always a very pleasant breeze.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: With se + indirect object (se le cayó), expresses accidental dropping.

examples.text: La lluvia cae sobre el tejado.
examples.trans: The rain falls on the tiled roof.

examples.text: Se me cayeron las monedas.
examples.trans: I accidentally dropped the coins.

meanings.note: Placed before the word it modifies.

examples.text: Ya son casi las doce.
examples.trans: It is almost twelve o'clock already.

examples.text: Casi olvido la llave en la mesa.
examples.trans: I nearly forgot the key on the table.

meanings.note: Onomatopoeia imitating the sound of something landing flat in water or mud.

examples.text: ¡Chof! El cartel cayó justo en medio del agua de la fuente.
examples.trans: Splash! The poster landed right in the middle of the fountain water.

examples.text: Las botas hicieron chof al pisar el charco del jardín.
examples.trans: The boots went squelch when stepping into the garden puddle.

coger.gloss: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)

meanings.en: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)
meanings.note: Standard everyday Peninsula Spanish verb for picking up objects or taking transport (g -> j before o: cojo).

examples.text: Cojo el autobús cada mañana.
examples.trans: I take the bus every morning.

examples.text: Coge una taza limpia del estante.
examples.trans: Take a clean cup from the shelf.

meanings.note: Unaccented como compares or gives a reason (distinct from interrogative cómo).

examples.text: Está fría como el agua del río.
examples.trans: It is as cold as river water.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works just as it should.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used for piano or guitar strings as well as rope.

examples.text: El macillo golpea tres cuerdas de acero a la vez.
examples.trans: The hammer strikes three steel strings at once.

examples.text: Esa cuerda central suena clara después de afinarla.
examples.trans: That middle string sounds clear after tuning it.

meanings.note: Con cuidado = carefully; ¡Cuidado con...! = Mind the...!

examples.text: El cuidado es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The care is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el cuidado.
examples.trans: We talk about the care.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: A la derecha / a mano derecha = on the right.

examples.text: La derecha está aquí.
examples.trans: The right is here.

examples.text: Vemos las derechas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rights from the door.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (salir directo = walk straight out).

examples.text: Es una pieza directa.
examples.trans: It is a direct piece.

examples.text: Sí, Rocío. Aunque dé media vuelta y salga directo por la puerta.
examples.trans: Yes, Rocio. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Ends in -e, so masculine and feminine forms are identical (un rollo enorme, una racha enorme).

examples.text: Acaba de entrar una racha enorme de viento por el arco de piedra.
examples.trans: A huge gust of wind just came in through the stone arch.

examples.text: Tomás trajo una cesta enorme llena de naranjas de Valencia.
examples.trans: Tomas brought an enormous basket full of Valencia oranges.

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Feminine form: la farmacéutica; works at la farmacia ('pharmacy').

examples.text: El farmacéutico de la esquina nos recomendó poner hielo.
examples.trans: The corner pharmacist recommended putting ice on it.

examples.text: La farmacéutica abre su tienda a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The pharmacist opens her shop at nine o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Festive hanging lantern strung across Spanish courtyards.

examples.text: El farolillo está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper lantern is here.

examples.text: Vemos los farolillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the paper lanterns from the door.

frente.gloss: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)

meanings.en: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)
meanings.note: La frente (f) = forehead; frente a frente = face to face.

examples.text: La frente está aquí.
examples.trans: The forehead is here.

examples.text: Vemos las frentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the foreheads from the door.

meanings.note: Means a stone water fountain in a square (una fuente de piedra), a large serving dish, or a source of information.

examples.text: La primera tarjeta muestra una fuente antigua de piedra.
examples.trans: The first card shows an old stone fountain.

examples.text: Nos sentamos a escuchar el agua junto a la fuente.
examples.trans: We sat listening to the water beside the fountain.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (llover/discutir fuerte).

examples.text: Es una pieza fuerte.
examples.trans: It is a strong piece.

examples.text: ¡Rápido, ciérralo! Vamos a subirlo... esperad, ¿qué es ese golpe metálico tan fuerte?
examples.trans: Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs... wait, what is that loud metallic bang?

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.text: ¿Dónde he dejado mis gafas?
examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?

examples.text: Lleva unas gafas redondas.
examples.trans: He wears round glasses.

meanings.note: Used both as a noun (el gigante) and as a two-form adjective (gigante / gigantes).

examples.text: Ernesto ha comprado un rollo gigante de papel blanco para el plano.
examples.trans: Ernesto bought a giant roll of white paper for the seating plan.

examples.text: Las olas parecían montañas gigantes desde el muro del puerto.
examples.trans: The waves looked like giant mountains from the harbour wall.

meanings.note: Gira a la izquierda = turn left.

examples.text: Gira a la izquierda después del puente.
examples.trans: Turn left after the bridge.

examples.text: Giró la llave dos veces con cuidado.
examples.trans: She turned the key twice carefully.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Indicates direction of movement or gaze.

examples.text: Camina hacia el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: Walk toward the stone bridge.

examples.text: Sigue mirando hacia la esquina.
examples.trans: Keep looking toward the corner.

meanings.note: Garden herbs or meadow grass.

examples.text: La hierba está aquí.
examples.trans: The herb is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hierbas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the herbs from the door.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va todo esta mañana?
examples.trans: How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: A la izquierda = on/to the left.

examples.text: La izquierda está aquí.
examples.trans: The left is here.

examples.text: Vemos las izquierdas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lefts from the door.

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.text: Siéntate junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: Sit next to the window.

examples.text: Trabajamos juntos en la posada.
examples.trans: We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Derived from lavar ('to wash'); tinta lavable means washable ink.

examples.text: Menos mal que Ernesto escribió el cartel con tinta azul lavable.
examples.trans: Thankfully Ernesto wrote the poster with washable blue ink.

examples.text: Estos manteles de algodón son resistentes y totalmente lavables.
examples.trans: These cotton tablecloths are durable and completely washable.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Terracotta or ceramic pot for courtyard plants and herbs.

examples.text: Regamos las macetas de hierbas cada mañana.
examples.trans: We water the herb pots every morning.

examples.text: Hay una maceta grande junto a la escalera de piedra.
examples.trans: There is a big plant pot beside the stone stairs.

meanings.note: Feminine despite ending in -o: la mano, las manos; a mano derecha = on your right-hand side.

examples.text: Gira después de la farmacia a mano derecha.
examples.trans: Turn past the pharmacy on your right-hand side.

examples.text: Tengo las manos limpias.
examples.trans: My hands are clean.

meanings.note: Ordinarily masculine in everyday speech (el mar Mediterráneo, salado como el mar), though poetic/seafaring Spanish also uses la mar.

examples.text: Esta cucharada del tarro blanco sabe salada como el mar.
examples.trans: This spoonful from the white jar tastes as salty as the sea.

examples.text: Desde la colina del parque se ve brillar el mar a lo lejos.
examples.trans: From the park hill you can see the sea shining in the distance.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas la sal, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Vivo aquí y trabajo aquí.
examples.trans: I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.text: Es una pieza media.
examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.text: La mesa está aquí.
examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: A woman baker is la panadera; the shop is la panadería.

examples.text: El panadero empieza a trabajar a las cuatro.
examples.trans: The baker starts work at four.

examples.text: La panadera nos guarda dos barras de pan.
examples.trans: The baker keeps two loaves of bread for us.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: El papel está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.text: La piedra está aquí.
examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint.

examples.text: La pintura es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The paint is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la pintura.
examples.trans: We talk about the paint.

meanings.note: Architectural drawing or city street map.

examples.text: El plano está aquí.
examples.trans: The blueprint is here.

examples.text: Vemos los planos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the blueprints from the door.

meanings.note: In Spanish LGBTQ+ and colloquial usage, 'tener pluma' or 'subirse de pluma' refers to noticeably campy or effeminate mannerisms.
Literal sense of the feminine noun 'la pluma'.

examples.text: pero se les sube de pluma, no... Sí.
examples.trans: but they get a bit too campy, right... Yes.

examples.text: Que se les sube mucho de pluma, dicen.
examples.trans: They say their campiness really comes out.

related.gloss: feather duster (in 'ver el plumero' = see someone's true colors)

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Used for a sudden gust of wind (una racha de viento) and a run of good or bad luck (una buena racha).

examples.text: Acaba de entrar una racha fresca de viento por el arco de la calle.
examples.trans: A cool gust of wind just came in through the street arch.

examples.text: El viernes por la tarde habrá rachas fuertes de viento de primavera.
examples.trans: On Friday afternoon there will be strong gusts of spring wind.

resistente.gloss: resistant; sturdy; durable (resistente al agua = waterproof)

meanings.en: resistant; sturdy; durable (resistente al agua = waterproof)
meanings.note: Ends in -e, so masculine and feminine forms are identical.

examples.text: La tinta de pluma es lavable, no es pintura resistente al agua.
examples.trans: Fountain-pen ink is washable, it is not waterproof paint.

examples.text: El roble antiguo del balcón es una madera muy resistente.
examples.trans: The old oak on the balcony is a very durable wood.

saltar.gloss: to jump; to spark / pop on

meanings.en: to jump; to spark / pop on
meanings.note: Ahí salta la llama = there goes the flame.

examples.text: El niño salta los charcos de lluvia.
examples.trans: The boy jumps over the rain puddles.

examples.text: De pronto saltó la chispa azul.
examples.trans: Suddenly the blue spark jumped on.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

secar.gloss: to dry; to wipe dry (secarse = to dry out)

meanings.en: to dry; to wipe dry (secarse = to dry out)
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (sequé, seque).

examples.text: Seca bien las bisagras antes de dar la pintura.
examples.trans: Dry the hinges thoroughly before applying paint.

examples.text: Con este sol la ropa tendida se seca enseguida.
examples.trans: In this sunshine the hanging laundry dries right away.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.text: Es una pieza segunda.
examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

examples.text: Un chupito para soltarte.
examples.trans: A shot to loosen you up.

examples.text: Suelta la maleta aquí.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase down here.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: sueño).

examples.text: Anoche soñé con un viaje en tren.
examples.trans: Last night I dreamed about a train journey.

examples.text: Siempre sueña con tener su propia cafetería.
examples.trans: She always dreams of having her own cafe.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Sujeta bien la linterna, por favor.
examples.trans: Hold the flashlight steady, please.

examples.text: Sujetó la nota con un clip metálico.
examples.trans: She clipped the note with a metal paperclip.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.text: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Tienen una habitación libre?
examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Con tinta permanente = in permanent ink.

examples.text: La tinta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The ink is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la tinta.
examples.trans: We talk about the ink.

meanings.note: Related to tirar ('to pull'); denotes a narrow strip of cloth, paper, tape, or lemon peel.

examples.text: Fijaos en la tira de tela blanca pegada alrededor de la tapa.
examples.trans: Look at the strip of white cloth stuck around the lid.

examples.text: Cortó la masa en tiras largas y finas.
examples.trans: She cut the dough into long, thin strips.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Shortens to un before masculine singular nouns.

examples.text: Toma uno recién salido del horno.
examples.trans: Take one fresh out of the oven.

examples.text: Contamos del uno al ocho.
examples.trans: We count from one to eight.

meanings.note: Light exclamation for a small slip or surprise.

examples.text: ¡Uy, casi se me cae la taza!
examples.trans: Oops, I nearly dropped the cup!

examples.text: ¡Uy, qué tarde es ya!
examples.trans: Oh my, how late it is already!

meanings.note: Homonym with two everyday meanings: a ship's canvas sail (vela de barco) and a wax candle (vela de cera).

examples.text: Con el viento del patio, el cartel tiraba como una vela de barco.
examples.trans: In the courtyard wind, the poster pulled like a boat's sail.

examples.text: Encendimos dos velas blancas sobre la mesa del piano al anochecer.
examples.trans: We lit two white candles on the piano table at nightfall.

volar.gloss: to fly; to sell out / disappear fast

meanings.en: to fly; to sell out / disappear fast
meanings.note: Stem changes o -> ue in stressed present forms (vuelo, vuelas, vuela, vuelan; subjunctive vuele, vuelen).

examples.text: El pan recién hecho vuela cada sábado por la mañana.
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread disappears fast every Saturday morning.

examples.text: Los pájaros vuelan sobre el limonero del patio.
examples.trans: Birds fly above the courtyard lemon tree.

volver.gloss: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

examples.text: Vuelvo en cinco minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in five minutes.

examples.text: Volvió a sonreír enseguida.
examples.trans: He smiled again right away.

vuelta.gloss: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)

meanings.en: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)
meanings.note: Dar una vuelta = take a stroll / make one turn.

examples.text: La vuelta está aquí.
examples.trans: The turn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vueltas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the turns from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

zas.gloss: whoosh!; zap!; bang! (sudden swift movement or blow)

meanings.en: whoosh!; zap!; bang! (sudden swift movement or blow)
meanings.note: Expressive onomatopoeia for a sudden gust of wind, quick snatch, or sharp impact.

examples.text: ¡Zas! Una racha de viento levantó las tarjetas de la mesa en un segundo.
examples.trans: Whoosh! A gust of wind lifted the cards off the table in a second.

examples.text: Cerró la puerta de golpe y ¡zas!, se apagó la vela.
examples.trans: He shut the door suddenly and whoosh!, the candle went out.

meanings.note: Plural los árboles.

examples.text: El árbol está aquí.
examples.trans: The tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los árboles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trees from the door.
